articles.title: Breaking Down Theo's Shock Moment in The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 and the Mystery of His Father With Actor Tyroe Muhafidin
articles.summary: A spoiler-filled The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 interview with Theo actor Tyroe Muhafidin.
body: Warning! Spoilers for The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 Episodes 1-4 follow.

If you’re caught up with The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, you’ll have watched Season 3, Episode 4 and were probably left reeling by a shock character death that leaves the elves in a spot of bother going into the final stretch.

During the first four episodes of Season 3, we see Theo, played by Tyroe Muhafidin, tempted by Sauron into becoming a Nazgnagôl. Nazgnagôl are men who wear one of Sauron’s Rings of Power, but still retain something of their humanity. That is, they are not fully Nazgûl, or Ringwraiths, as we know of the beings in the Third Age of J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth. They are, at this stage, Ring Servants.

Theo, last seen as a hopeful child of the Southlands and friend of hero elf Arondir, is now older and full of hate after five years of Númenórean oppression. Sauron sees something in him, something special, and offers Theo a gift. In Episode 2, appropriately called The Gift of Men, Sauron performs a dark ritual that lets Theo “meet” his mysterious father, or at least that’s what we think is happening here (with Sauron, you never really know!).
points: A spoiler-filled The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 interview with Theo actor Tyroe Muhafidin.

articles.title: This 3D Pet SIM You Never Played Has Over 12,000 ‘Overwhelmingly Positive’ Reviews
articles.summary: Have you ever wanted to raise your own genetically mutated pup? Well, there's a Steam game focused on exactly that, and it probably deserves more success than it's managed in the four years since it launched.
body: It's as much a comedic game as it is a simulator, for two reasons. Firstly, the dogs look ridiculous. They're made up of an amalgamation of shapes, including lengthy, cuboid torsos and enormous tails, somewhat reminiscent of the creatures in the early noughties British children's show Bamzooki.

Secondly, Wobbledogs has some wacky physics in play, which means it's a good laugh just observing your pets. "Two dogs with separate body structures will experience the world in different ways," reads the "about this game" section on Steam.

Impressively, each Wobbledog also has a simulated genetics system. "As they age, they periodically enter a pupal state and physically mutate. The foods they eat fill their guts with different flora… [which] influence the dogs' mutations, letting you craft and mold them to fit your own idea of canine (im)perfection!"

Wobbledogs is very much a make-your-own-fun sort of game though, so there are no explicit goals other than enjoying yourself. You can create and design habitats for your dogs, and you'll unlock more cosmetic decorations and objects as you play. "Give your dogs a relaxing place to sleep, set up a maze, or even cultivate a garden."
points: Have you ever wanted to raise your own genetically mutated pup?
Well, there's a Steam game focused on exactly that, and it probably deserves more success than it's managed in the four years since it launched.

articles.title: Vice City was the GTA that established Rockstar's killer formula - and 24 years on, it's still one of the best games ever made
articles.summary: "Get the limey out of here," Burt Reynolds tells the producers of GTA: Vice City during a recording session for the game, as Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser enters the studio.
body: I can't verify the truth of this story. It's one of those development rumours that's been around for a long time, originally written in a book about how games conquered pop culture called "All Your Base Are Belong to Us" by Harold Goldberg. But I like to believe it's true, because in this one moment, the two crucial strands of GTA: Vice City's DNA helix together: its star power and Rockstar's arrogance.

And I'm not saying that in a pejorative way at all. I think a game of Vice City's scope - stretched to breaking with ambition, budget, and technical wizardry - couldn't exist without the ego trip of Rockstar at its highest. This is a game that (somehow!) started as a bit of DLC for GTA 3, supposedly intended to launch as a mission pack when Rockstar North figured out how to port it to PC. GTA 3 launched in October 2001, and by some miracle - and lots of crunch, no doubt - Vice City hit shelves in October 2002.

articles.title: Apple's Sci-Fi Thriller Masterpiece Has One of the Best Seasons in TV History
articles.summary: In 2022, Apple was three years into its streaming experiment and still trying to find its footing. Aside from Ted Lasso, the tech giant hadn't released any breakout hits. And while a few sci-fi shows like For All Mankind and Foundation had fans, they weren't exactly mainstream success stories.
body: Dan Erickson and Ben Stiller didn't just change Apple TV with Severance, which firmly established the streamer as the home for groundbreaking new sci-fi. They also delivered a perfectly timed anti-work masterpiece at exactly the right time, tapping into the cultural zeitgeist with a perfect season of television that still hasn't been surpassed (even by the show's own very good second season).

While both seasons of Severance are phenomenal, it’s hard to describe how expertly Erickson’s first nine-episode season conveys the despair of the “work-first” attitude prevalent in modern society. Erickson, who worked in a literal door factory while writing early versions of the series, takes that attitude to its most literal extreme: imagining a dystopian future where companies surgically split their employees' consciousness to create an "innie" who knows only work and an "outie" who has no idea what their own job entails.

articles.title: 20 Years Ago, the Best Sci-Fi Show of the Century Delivered the Most Epic Space Battle in TV History
articles.summary: Two decades later, this spectacle from Battlestar Galactica season 3’s “Exodus, Part 2” remains unforgettable sci-fi TV. It’s dazzling and horrifying, and still one of the coolest things ever broadcast on science-fiction television.
body: To liberate the humans trapped under Cylon occupation, Admiral William Adama (Edward James Olmos) jumps the titular Battlestar Galactica directly into the atmosphere of New Caprica. The warship plummets toward the settlement and deploys Viper fighter jets amidst the chaos before jumping back into space moments before it would have crashed, likely obliterating the planet on impact.

Minutes later, while the Galactica is damaged and surrounded by enemy ships, Lee Adama (Jamie Bamber) arrives aboard the Pegasus. He buys his father enough time to escape, evacuates his own crew, and transforms the most advanced remaining warship in humanity's fleet into an enormous battering ram. Pegasus tears through one Cylon basestar, explodes, and sends a flaming flight pod spinning into another. It’s both a spectacular death scene and the decisive blow in the battle to liberate New Caprica.
points: Two decades later, this spectacle from Battlestar Galactica season 3’s “Exodus, Part 2” remains unforgettable sci-fi TV.

articles.title: James Gunn Shuts Down Rumors That Skydance Is Meddling With Man of Tomorrow
articles.summary: James Gunn has shut down rumors that the new DC overseers at Skydance have meddled with his cut of Man of Tomorrow following his shocking DC Studios exit. The internet has filled with gossip in the wake of Gunn and Peter Safran's departure as co-chairmen of the comic book entertainment wing earlier…
body: These are just some of the accusations that Gunn sought to dispel in a Threads post tonight. In what is essentially his first public statement since leaving DC Studios, the filmmaker took aim at the gossip that has DCU fans concerned. Not only have "sweeping changes" to Man of Tomorrow not been made, but apparently, no one at Skydance has even seen his movie yet.

"There are a lot of untrue rumors going around, but one of them is that Skydance has seen Man of Tomorrow and that all sorts of sweeping changes are being made," he said. "No one from Skydance has even seen the movie - the only people that have are Peter Safran and a very small trusted group of friends and family. So any stories around this narrative are false."

It's a response that will not answer every question comic book movie enjoyers have about the future of the DCU, but it does clear the air about much of the more damning chatter online. Gunn's comments mean that any talk of Skydance being unhappy with the current cut of Man of Tomorrow is false. It also sounds like, at least for now, Supergirl and Blue Beetle, who had been previously reported to return, are safe.
points: James Gunn has shut down rumors that the new DC overseers at Skydance have meddled with his cut of Man of Tomorrow following his shocking DC Studios exit.

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering animated series Planeswalker is coming to Netflix in 2027
articles.summary: Netflix's long-gestating Magic: The Gathering animated series is called Planeswalker, and it's coming in 2027.
body: According to a synopsis shared with IGN, the series follows Chandra Nalaar, "a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts, and haunted by her past". It continues: "Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence".

Netflix first announced a Magic: The Gathering series in June 2019, with Avengers: Endgame directors Joe and Anthony Russo attached, and it was originally due in late 2022. Two years in, the original showrunners departed over creative differences, and in September 2024, Netflix confirmed it had started again from scratch with Star Trek: Picard and 12 Monkeys showrunner Terry Matalas in charge.
IGN reports that Matalas, who most recently ran Marvel's VisionQuest, is running the show alongside Cindy Appel. Budapest-based studio DIGIC Pictures is handling the animation.
At the end of last month, we learned PUBG is also being turned into a live-action series for Netflix, with Donald Glover set to direct, write, executive produce, and star.

articles.title: “Physical” GTA 6 Copies Might Be Vulnerable To A Very Stupid But Serious Trick
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 ditched traditional discs for its "physical" launch, with Rockstar's game being sold as a digital code-in-box at retailers beginning this week. However, it appears a packaging choice may have accidentally left the game vulnerable to thieves--assuming they have a flashlight.
body: As shared on the forum ResetEra, users who received a physical version of Grand Theft Auto 6, at least in PEGI regions, report that the game's download code is printed directly on the inside of the cover rather than on a card or separate insert. When a flashlight is focused on the cover from the outside of the closed game case, the download code is visible in reverse.
In other words, there's a serious risk people could go into a store, do this trick, redeem the code, and leave the poor soul who actually buys the game off the shelf without GTA 6.

At this time, the trick does not seem to work on North American copies of GTA 6, as the code is intentionally obscured. Why Rockstar would not use this strategy on all regions is unclear. We've reached out to Rockstar for an explanation and will update this post if and when we receive a response.

If you happen to get your GTA 6 code stolen after paying $80, you can at least sleep soundly knowing that the thief can't play the game yet. Code-in-box copies, as well as digital preorders, all unlock for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.

articles.title: GTA 6 Owner Take-Two Is Not Interested In Selling Itself After EA Goes Private For $55 Billion
articles.summary: Recently, the gaming giant Electronic Arts was taken private in a $55 billion sale to an investor consortium led by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. Could GTA 6 owner Take-Two be the next big company that gets acquired? Don't bet on it, CEO Strauss Zelnick says.
body: Speaking to David Rubenstein, Zelnick said Take-Two's business results have proven that it "can do very well as an independent company."
He said Take-Two's business is already "at scale" and healthy enough financially with a "terrific balance sheet," as he put it.
"We are not in a place where we need to be part of a bigger organization to be competitive. And in the entertainment business, scale matters," he said.

Zelnick said companies that do less than a billion in annual revenue might have issues with developing, marketing, and distributing games at scale. Not only that, but companies that don't generate a lot of money might not be able to survive the realities of the creative business, in which sometimes your product flops.

articles.title: Interest in The Legend of Zelda was "getting smaller and smaller" before Breath of the Wild, according to former Nintendo marketing leads
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild gave the beloved series a massive second wind, according to two former Nintendo marketing leads.
body: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 's most recent remake has been a mega success, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game so far, but the shiny new adventure has also prompted some online debate over where the series should go next. Should Zelda lean into its carefully directed history - like the one brilliantly remade in Ocarina of Time - or keep the ball rolling with Breath of the Wild's wide open, spontaneous sandbox?

Nintendo of America 's ex-director of social media marketing Kit Ellis and former public relations manager Krysta Yang chimed in on the discourse in their latest podcast (below), and explained that Zelda wasn't doing too hot before the Switch era.

"There has been some revisionist history out there lately," Ellis said in response to fans who reckon "the Zelda team ripped away" series staples, like classic dungeons and linear worlds, at the height of their popularity.
The Legend of Zelda was supposedly "shrinking," while "interest in the audience was getting smaller and smaller" with each new entry. "They had to do something dramatic," Ellis said.
points: The Legend of Zelda was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild gave the beloved series a massive second wind, according to two former Nintendo marketing leads.
